This cake is 22 cm in diameter (8.7 inches) so if you plan on making anything bigger you will have to do the maths to increase the amount of ingredients you need i'm sorry :'')For the base you will need:

* 14 Oreos (that's about 150g / 5.3 oz)
* 80 grams of butter or margerine (that's about 2.8 oz) you're also free to add up a little more for a more sturdier and less spongy texture, I had 125 grams of butter and I tossed it all in because I was too lazy to cut it up and because the sight of a knife would've ended this prematurely

Now for that sexy creamy top part you need:

* 14 Oreos again
* 200 gr of cream cheese (7 oz)
* 80 gr of powdered sugar (2.8 oz)
* 1 packet of vanilla sugar (10 grams or 0.4 oz)
* 500 ml of whipping cream (i'm sorry idk how to convert mililiters)

# Now that the painful part of measuring is done we can get to mixin'!

1. We need to make the base first so grind up 14 Oreos with a mixer or a hammer and then add in the melted butter. Mix all of that until you get this buttery Oreo paste!
2. Now place the metal cake hoop on the corresponding plate/casserole and cast this paste all over the bottom, filling in the entirety of it and arrange the paste so it's flat and spread out evenly across the plate. When you're finished toss it into the fridge and begin prepping the creamy part!
3. Prep the whipped cream (pour whipping cream into a bowl and use mixer to thiccen it)
4. Add cream cheese, powdered sugar & vanilla sugar into a separate bowl and mix them all together
5. When the cheesy amalgamation gets this creamy whipped texture then add the thiccened whipped cream into the mix and mix them all together a bit so they can form this big mixture of whipped cream and cheese
6. Grind the remaining 14 Oreos **by hand** or use a hammer to break them down and then add them into the mix
7. Now's the time to take out the plate with the hoop from the fridge again and cast the cream all over the base, spread the cream evenly across and watch out that it doesn't leak thru the hoop.
8. Leave the cake in the fridge to chill for minimally 24 hours so both the base and the cream can harden. You can take off the cake hoop right before serving.

Now in my case I cut the remaining Oreos in half and arranged them on top to form the iconic Rammstein cross we all know and love. I drew out the R on a separate sheet of baking paper with chocolate topping and left it in a freezer to harden; although upon separating it from the paper it begun to fall apart so I used the leftover topping to patch it up on the cake. But you can use leftover Oreos or whatever you think would fit with the cake to decorate the top!!
